facts.raw_span: a mass in the right nostril that had been growing for about 1 year
The lesion bled with minimal trauma
did not obstruct his breathing
The patient did not smoke
denied any medical history of chronic rhinosinusitis
a 1-cm, nontender, exophytic, verrucous, skin-colored plaque on the right nasal vestibule
Papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores that are lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium
Shows mucin-containing goblet cells
Neither cytologic atypia nor atypical mitotic figures are present
An exophytic, verrucous, and skin-colored plaque on the right nasal vestibule

concepts.why: The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and mucin-containing goblet cells, without cytologic atypia or atypical mitotic figures, is consistent with inverted papilloma.
The exophytic, verrucous, skin-colored plaque with papillary fronds and nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium is consistent with squamous papilloma.
The presence of a verrucous, skin-colored plaque on the right nasal vestibule is consistent with Verrucous Carcinoma.

rationales.F01: A mass in the right nostril is more typical of inverted papilloma and squamous papilloma.
rationales.F06: The description of the plaque is highly suggestive of inverted papilloma and squamous papilloma.
rationales.F07: Papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores are characteristic of inverted papilloma.
rationales.F08: Mucin-containing goblet cells are often seen in inverted papilloma.
rationales.F09: The absence of cytologic atypia or atypical mitotic figures rules out verrucous carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The clinical presentation is consistent with inverted papilloma and squamous papilloma.
